examples.en: The company computers have a firewall installed.

examples.ko: 방화벽 때문에 그 사이트가 열리지 않아요.
examples.en: That site won't open because of the firewall.

examples.ko: 새 방화벽을 켜고 나서 해킹 시도가 줄었어요.
examples.en: Hacking attempts dropped after I turned on the new firewall.

examples.ko: 집 공유기에도 기본 방화벽 기능이 들어 있대요.
examples.en: I heard even a home router has a basic firewall function.

examples.ko: 방화벽 설정만 바꾸면 게임이 잘 연결될 거예요.
examples.en: The game should connect well if you just change the firewall settings.

examples.ko: 방화벽에 막혀서 필요한 프로그램을 쓸 수 없었어요.
examples.en: I couldn't use the program I needed because the firewall blocked it.

explain: 컴퓨터 보안 이야기에서 주로 나오는 말이에요. '방화벽을 켜다/끄다', '방화벽에 막히다'처럼 써요. 건물에서 불이 번지는 걸 막는 벽도 같은 이름이지만, 요즘은 거의 컴퓨터 쪽을 가리켜요.
explain_en: This word mostly comes up in computer security. People say '방화벽을 켜다/끄다' (turn the firewall on/off) and '방화벽에 막히다' (get blocked by the firewall). The same word names a wall that stops fire from spreading in a building, but today it mostly means the computer kind.

examples.en: Who holds the patent for this technology?
He was designated a holder of intangible cultural heritage.
I met a world record holder in person.

examples.ko: 면허 보유자만 이 차를 운전할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only license holders can drive this car.
That company is the holder of many patents.
They give a discount to cardholders.

explain: '기록 보유자', '자격증 보유자'처럼 앞에 가진 것을 붙여 써요. 물건을 가진 평범한 주인은 '주인'이나 '소유자'라고 해요. 회사나 나라는 '보유 기업', '보유국'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: You put what someone holds in front, as in '기록 보유자' (record holder) or '자격증 보유자' (certificate holder). For an ordinary owner of an object, people say '주인' or '소유자'. For companies and countries, they say '보유 기업' and '보유국'.

examples.en: I fell and broke my collarbone.
I was complimented on how nice my collarbone line looks.

examples.ko: 의사가 쇄골을 눌러 보고 아프냐고 물었어요.
examples.en: The doctor pressed on my collarbone and asked if it hurt.
The area between my shoulder and collarbone keeps feeling stiff.
The bag strap presses on my collarbone and it's uncomfortable.

examples.ko: 쇄골뼈는 가슴 위쪽에 가로로 길게 있어요.
examples.en: The collarbone runs long and horizontal across the upper chest.

explain: 병원 이야기와 몸매 이야기에서 많이 쓰고, 일상에서는 '쇄골뼈'라고도 해요. '쇄골이 부러지다', '쇄골이 드러나다'처럼 써요. '어깨', '목'은 훨씬 넓은 부분을 가리켜서 쇄골과 달라요.
explain_en: It shows up in medical talk and in talk about body shape, and people also say '쇄골뼈'. Common combinations are '쇄골이 부러지다' (the collarbone breaks) and '쇄골이 드러나다' (the collarbone shows). '어깨' and '목' cover a much wider area than 쇄골.

examples.ko: 이 드라마의 원작자는 유명한 웹툰 작가예요.
examples.en: The original author of this drama is a famous webtoon artist.
The original author even wrote the film script personally.

examples.ko: 영화가 원작자의 뜻과 달라서 논란이 됐어요.
examples.en: The film caused controversy because it differed from the original author's intent.

examples.ko: 노래를 쓰려면 원작자에게 허락을 받아야 해요.
examples.en: To use the song, you have to get permission from the original creator.
I want to meet the original author and hear their story.

examples.ko: 영상 설명에 원작자 이름이 적혀 있어요.
examples.en: The original creator's name is written in the video description.

explain: 소설, 만화, 노래처럼 처음 만든 사람을 말할 때 써요. 영화나 드라마로 바뀐 작품에서 '원작'은 작품, '원작자'는 그 작품을 쓴 사람이에요. 그냥 글쓴이는 '작가', 그림을 그린 사람은 '화가'라고 해요.
explain_en: It names the person who first created a novel, comic, or song. For a work adapted into a film or drama, '원작' is the work and '원작자' is the person who wrote it. A plain writer is '작가', and someone who paints is a '화가'.

examples.en: This is my first Lunar New Year in a foreign land.
The scenery of that distant land was as beautiful as a photo.

examples.ko: 이국적인 음식을 먹으러 새 가게에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to a new restaurant to eat exotic food.

examples.ko: 여행을 가서 이국 사람들과 금방 친해졌어요.
examples.en: On my trip I quickly became friends with people from another country.

examples.ko: 그 카페는 분위기가 이국 느낌이라 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: That cafe is popular because it has an exotic feel.
I lived alone in a foreign land for a long time.

explain: '이국'은 글이나 노래에서 주로 보여요. 말할 때는 '외국'이 훨씬 자연스러워요. '이국적이다'는 낯설고 신선한 분위기를 칭찬할 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: '이국' appears mostly in writing and songs. In speech, '외국' sounds far more natural. '이국적이다' is often used to praise a place or look that feels unfamiliar and fresh.

examples.en: I cycled all the way around Jeju Island.
Traveling around the world is my dream.

examples.ko: 내년에 배낭을 메고 유럽을 일주할 거예요.
examples.en: Next year I'll tour around Europe with a backpack.

examples.ko: 친구와 섬을 일주하고 나서 맛집에 갔어요.
examples.en: After going around the island with a friend, we went to a great restaurant.
Even by bus, one day is enough to go all the way around.

examples.ko: 호수를 일주해 보니 생각보다 길이 험했어요.
examples.en: After going around the lake, I found the path rougher than I expected.

explain: '제주도 일주', '세계 일주'처럼 큰 곳을 한 바퀴 크게 도는 여행에 써요. 동네를 한 바퀴 도는 건 '돌다', '산책하다'를 써요. 보통 '일주를 하다'보다 '일주하다'로 붙여 말해요.
explain_en: It is used for a trip that goes once all the way around a large place, as in '제주도 일주' or '세계 일주'. Walking around a neighborhood is '돌다' or '산책하다'. People usually say '일주하다' as one word rather than '일주를 하다'.

examples.en: The lock is rusty and the key won't go in.
I put a small lock on the drawer.
Lock your bike to the pole with a lock.
I forgot the lock's combination.

examples.ko: 가방 지퍼에 채운 자물쇠는 열쇠로 열어요.
examples.en: I open the lock on my bag's zipper with a key.

examples.ko: 대문에 자물쇠가 잠겨 있어서 들어갈 수 없었어요.
examples.en: The gate was padlocked, so I couldn't get in.

explain: 자물쇠는 잠그는 쪽, 열쇠는 여는 쪽이라서 '자물쇠와 열쇠'로 짝을 이뤄 말해요. '자물쇠를 채우다', '자물쇠를 열다'처럼 써요. 문을 여닫을 때 잡는 부분은 '문고리'나 '손잡이'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 이건 비밀이니까 입에 자물쇠를 채워 주세요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말하지 않고 비밀을 지킨다는 뜻이에요. 부탁하거나 다짐할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means to say nothing and keep a secret. People use it when asking someone to stay quiet or when promising to.

explain_en: A 자물쇠 is the part that locks, and a 열쇠 is the key that opens it, so the two are often said together as '자물쇠와 열쇠'. Common phrases are '자물쇠를 채우다' (put on a lock) and '자물쇠를 열다' (open a lock). The part you grab to open and close a door is the '문고리' or '손잡이'.

examples.ko: 이 영화의 제작비는 백억 원이 넘어요.
examples.en: This film's production cost is over ten billion won.
We postponed filming because the budget fell short.

examples.ko: 제작비를 줄이려고 장면을 몇 개 뺐어요.
examples.en: To cut production costs, they removed a few scenes.

examples.ko: 광고 영상 제작비를 먼저 알아보고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm first checking how much an ad video would cost to make.

examples.ko: 적은 제작비로도 좋은 작품을 만들 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can make a good work even on a small budget.
I heard season 2 was canceled because of the production cost.

explain: 영화, 드라마, 영상, 책처럼 작품을 만드는 데 드는 돈에 써요. 공장에서 물건을 만드는 돈은 '생산비'나 '원가'를 더 많이 써요. '제작비를 들이다', '제작비가 들다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is used for the money spent making a work such as a film, drama, video, or book. For the cost of making goods in a factory, '생산비' or '원가' is more common. Common phrases are '제작비를 들이다' (spend production money) and '제작비가 들다' (production costs arise).

examples.ko: 그 단체의 조직원이 천 명이 넘어요.
examples.en: That group has more than a thousand members.
A notice went out saying they're recruiting new members.
The members meet every Monday.

examples.ko: 경찰이 범죄 조직원 세 명을 붙잡았어요.
examples.en: The police caught three members of a criminal organization.
The union first asked its members for their opinions.

examples.ko: 그는 조직원으로서 맡은 일을 열심히 했어요.
examples.en: As a member, he worked hard at the task he was given.

explain: 뉴스에서는 범죄 조직이나 정치 단체의 사람을 말할 때 많이 나와요. 회사나 모임 사람은 '직원', '회원', '구성원'이 자연스러워요. 일상 대화에서는 거의 쓰지 않는 편이에요.
explain_en: In the news it mostly refers to people in a criminal or political organization. For people in a company or club, '직원', '회원', or '구성원' sound more natural. It is rarely used in everyday conversation.

examples.ko: 직감으로 이 길이 아니라는 걸 알았어요.
examples.en: I sensed by instinct that this wasn't the right road.
My hunch was right.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 거짓말을 한다는 직감이 들었어요.
examples.en: I had a feeling that person was lying.
I trusted my gut and went into that shop.

examples.ko: 엄마의 직감은 정말 무서울 만큼 정확해요.
examples.en: My mom's intuition is scarily accurate.
Going with my hunch, I contacted them first.

explain: 이유를 따지기 전에 먼저 오는 느낌이에요. '육감'도 비슷하고, 편하게 말할 때는 '촉'이라고도 해요. '직감이 들다', '직감이 맞다/틀리다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is the feeling that comes before you reason things out. '육감' is similar, and in casual speech people also say '촉'. Common phrases are '직감이 들다' (get a hunch) and '직감이 맞다/틀리다' (the hunch is right/wrong).

examples.ko: 문 앞에서 나쁜 일이 생겼다고 직감했어요.
examples.en: At the door I sensed something bad had happened.

examples.ko: 아이는 엄마가 화났다는 걸 직감하고 조용해졌어요.
examples.en: The child sensed Mom was angry and went quiet.

examples.ko: 저는 처음 만났을 때 이 사람과 오래 갈 거라고 직감했어요.
examples.en: When we first met, I had a feeling we'd last a long time.
He has a great ability to sense danger.

examples.ko: 이렇게 조용한 걸 보면 뭔가 있다는 걸 직감할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Seeing how quiet it is, you can tell something is up.

examples.ko: 사장님은 일이 잘못됐다고 직감한 듯 얼굴이 굳었어요.
examples.en: The boss's face stiffened as if he sensed something had gone wrong.

explain: '느끼다'보다 이유 없이 딱 알아챈다는 느낌이 강해요. 알아챈 내용을 앞에 붙여 '~다고 직감하다', '~임을 직감하다'처럼 말해요. 명사 '직감'을 써서 '직감이 들다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: Compared with '느끼다', it carries a stronger sense of knowing something right away without a reason. You put what you sensed in front, as in '~다고 직감하다' or '~임을 직감하다'. You can also use the noun: '직감이 들다'.

examples.en: In autumn, farmers harvest the rice.

examples.ko: 우리 할아버지는 올해도 직접 쌀을 추수하셨어요.
examples.en: My grandfather harvested the rice himself again this year.

examples.ko: 비가 오기 전에 서둘러 추수해야 해요.
examples.en: We have to hurry and harvest before the rain comes.
After the harvest, the village holds a feast.

examples.ko: 추수할 때가 되자 들판이 노랗게 변했어요.
examples.en: When it was time to harvest, the fields turned yellow.

examples.ko: 다 추수한 논이 텅 비어 보여요.
examples.en: The fully harvested paddy looks empty.

explain: '추수하다'는 가을에 벼 같은 곡식을 거둘 때 써요. '수확하다'는 곡식뿐 아니라 과일과 채소에도 두루 써요. 명사 '추수'로 '추수가 끝나다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: '추수하다' is for gathering grain such as rice in autumn. '수확하다' works more broadly, also covering fruit and vegetables. You can also use the noun and say '추수가 끝나다' (the harvest is over).

examples.en: This player has excellent dribbling technique.
I learned a new makeup technique.

examples.ko: 기본 테크닉만 익히면 누구나 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Anyone can do it once they master the basic technique.

examples.ko: 피아노는 어려운 테크닉이 많이 필요한 악기예요.
examples.en: The piano is an instrument that needs a lot of difficult technique.

examples.ko: 그는 화려한 테크닉으로 관객을 놀라게 했어요.
examples.en: He amazed the audience with flashy technique.
I think speaking has its techniques too.

explain: '기술'보다 가볍고 실용적인 요령에 가까워요. 운동, 화장, 요리, 연주에서 손이나 몸으로 하는 기술을 말할 때 많이 써요. 큰 산업 분야의 기술은 '기술'이나 '기술력'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It feels lighter and more practical than '기술', closer to a knack. It is common for skills done by hand or body in sports, makeup, cooking, and music. For big industrial technology, people say '기술' or '기술력'.

examples.ko: 한국에서는 학연과 지연이 중요하다는 말이 있어요.
examples.en: In Korea, people say school ties and hometown ties matter.
A rumor went around that he got promoted because of school ties.
We came from the same school, so we grew close through that tie.

examples.ko: 채용은 학연이 아니라 실력으로 해야 해요.
examples.en: Hiring should be based on ability, not school ties.
He worked without playing up his school connections.

examples.ko: 학연에 얽매이지 않는 회사를 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a company that isn't bound by school ties.

explain: 같은 학교를 나와서 생기는 인연이에요. 한국에서는 '학연, 지연, 혈연'을 한 묶음으로 자주 말하고, '학연으로 뽑다'처럼 불공평하다는 비판의 느낌이 있어요. 좋은 뜻으로는 '동문', '선후배'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is the connection formed by attending the same school. Koreans often group '학연, 지연, 혈연' (school, hometown, family ties) together, and '학연으로 뽑다' carries a tone of criticism about unfairness. For a positive meaning, '동문' or '선후배' sounds more natural.

examples.en: I filled a basin with water and washed my hands.

examples.ko: 빨래를 큰 대야에서 발로 밟아 빨았어요.
examples.en: I washed the laundry in a big basin by stepping on it.
It's handy to have a small basin.

examples.ko: 물이 넘치지 않게 대야를 조심히 들었어요.
examples.en: I carried the basin carefully so the water wouldn't spill.

examples.ko: 비가 새서 방 안에 대야로 물을 받았어요.
examples.en: The roof leaked, so I caught the water in a basin inside the room.
This basin is plastic, so it's light.

explain: '세숫대야'처럼 앞에 용도를 붙여 말하는 일이 많아요. 부엌에서 음식을 섞을 때는 '양푼'이나 '볼'을 쓰고, 씻거나 빨래할 때는 '대야'를 써요. 요즘은 수도에서 바로 씻어서 예전만큼 자주 보이지 않아요.
explain_en: People often add the purpose in front, as in '세숫대야' (face-washing basin). In the kitchen, a mixing bowl is '양푼' or '볼', while '대야' is for washing and laundry. Because people now wash straight at the tap, you see it less than before.

en: touch each other; be in contact

examples.en: I looked at the place where the sky and sea meet.

examples.ko: 두 집의 담이 서로 맞닿아 있어요.
examples.en: The walls of the two houses touch each other.
My heart raced the moment our fingertips touched.

examples.ko: 우리 방은 옆집 벽과 맞닿고 있어서 소리가 잘 들려요.
examples.en: Our room shares a wall with the next house, so sounds carry easily.
Cups make a sound when they touch each other.

examples.ko: 책상 두 개를 맞닿을 만큼 가깝게 붙여 놓았어요.
examples.en: I put two desks so close that they touch.

explain: 둘이 서로 끝이 닿을 때 써서 '서로 맞닿다'처럼 자주 말해요. 한쪽이 상대에게 닿는 건 '닿다', 아예 붙어 버린 건 '붙다'를 써요. 소리는 [맏따타]로 나요.
explain_en: It is used when two things touch end to end, so '서로 맞닿다' (touch each other) is a common phrase. When only one side reaches the other, use '닿다'; when they are completely stuck together, use '붙다'. It is pronounced [맏따타].

examples.en: Grandmother has become very frail.
My body is weak from a long illness.

examples.ko: 의사가 쇠약한 아이에게 영양제를 먹이라고 했어요.
examples.en: The doctor said to give the frail child supplements.
I pushed myself too hard and my health declined.
Being frail, he finds even climbing stairs hard.

examples.ko: 몸이 쇠약하다고 해서 일찍 쉬게 했어요.
examples.en: Since his body was weak, we let him rest early.

explain: 건강이나 체력이 오래 약해진 상태에 써요. 그냥 힘이 없는 건 '약하다', 잠깐 지친 건 '피곤하다'예요. '체력이 쇠약하다', '신경쇠약'처럼 쓰지만 말할 때는 '약해지다'가 더 흔해요.
explain_en: It describes health or strength that has been weak for a long time. Simply lacking strength is '약하다', and being briefly worn out is '피곤하다'. It appears in '체력이 쇠약하다' and '신경쇠약', but in speech '약해지다' is more common.

examples.en: I mended the pants that had a hole.
The dry cleaner's will alter and mend clothes for you.
I went to have my jeans hemmed.

examples.ko: 낡은 구두를 수선하면 더 오래 신을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you repair old shoes, you can wear them longer.

examples.ko: 이 가방 끈은 수선할 수 있는지 물어봤어요.
examples.en: I asked if the strap on this bag can be repaired.
Mom mended the ripped blanket herself.

explain: 옷, 신발, 가방처럼 천이나 가죽으로 된 물건을 고칠 때 써요. 기계나 전자 제품은 '고치다'나 '수리하다'를 써서 '수선'은 맞지 않아요. 옷을 맡길 때는 '수선을 맡기다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used for fixing items made of fabric or leather, such as clothes, shoes, and bags. For machines and electronics, use '고치다' or '수리하다' instead; '수선' doesn't fit. When you hand over clothes for fixing, you say '수선을 맡기다'.

examples.en: After the exams, a study slump hit me.
Every athlete goes through a slump.
I went on a trip to get out of my slump.
I'm in a slump lately and don't feel like doing anything.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 긴 슬럼프 끝에 새 앨범을 냈어요.
examples.en: That singer released a new album after a long slump.
A friend helped me when I fell into a slump.

explain: 운동, 공부, 일이 한동안 잘 안 되는 시기에 써요. 그냥 기분이 안 좋은 건 '우울하다'이고, 슬럼프는 성과가 떨어질 때 말해요. '슬럼프가 오다', '슬럼프에 빠지다', '슬럼프를 극복하다'처럼 같이 쓰는 말이 정해져 있어요.
explain_en: It is for a period when sports, study, or work stops going well for a while. Just feeling down is '우울하다'; 슬럼프 is used when your results drop. It pairs with fixed verbs: '슬럼프가 오다' (a slump comes), '슬럼프에 빠지다' (fall into a slump), '슬럼프를 극복하다' (overcome a slump).

examples.ko: 당뇨가 있는 사람은 인슐린 주사를 맞아요.
examples.en: People with diabetes take insulin shots.
When there isn't enough insulin, blood sugar rises.
The doctor prescribed insulin for me.

examples.ko: 인슐린은 몸에서 혈당을 조절하는 역할을 해요.
examples.en: Insulin plays a role in controlling blood sugar in the body.
I carry an insulin pen in my bag.

examples.ko: 저녁 먹기 전에 인슐린으로 혈당을 맞춰요.
examples.en: Before dinner, I adjust my blood sugar with insulin.

explain: '당뇨', '혈당'과 늘 같이 나오는 의학 단어예요. '인슐린 주사', '인슐린 저항성', '인슐린이 나오다'처럼 써요. 일상 대화에서는 본인이나 가족이 당뇨일 때 주로 들어요.
explain_en: This medical word almost always appears with '당뇨' (diabetes) and '혈당' (blood sugar). It is used in '인슐린 주사' (insulin shot), '인슐린 저항성' (insulin resistance), and '인슐린이 나오다' (insulin is secreted). In daily talk you mostly hear it when you or a family member has diabetes.

examples.en: I found old newspapers in the school resource room.
Reports and photos are organized in the resource room.

examples.ko: 필요한 파일은 회사 자료실에 올려 두세요.
examples.en: Please upload the files you need to the company's resource section.

examples.ko: 도서관 자료실이 몇 시에 문을 열어요?
examples.en: What time does the library's reference room open?
I went to the reference room and copied an old article.

examples.ko: 자료실 컴퓨터는 학생들이 자유롭게 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: Students can freely use the computers in the resource room.

explain: '자료실'은 건물 안의 방뿐 아니라 웹사이트 메뉴 이름으로도 많이 써서, 파일을 올리고 받는 곳을 가리켜요. 책을 빌리는 곳은 '대출실', 조용히 공부하는 곳은 '열람실'이에요.
explain_en: '자료실' is not only a room in a building; it is also a very common website menu name for the place where files are uploaded and downloaded. The place to borrow books is '대출실', and the quiet study area is '열람실'.

en: establish oneself as; take one's place as

examples.en: That singer established herself as a national singer.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 학습 서비스 분야에서 자리매김하고 있어요.
examples.en: This app is establishing its position in the learning service field.

examples.ko: 새 브랜드가 시장에 자리매김하기까지 삼 년이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took three years for the new brand to establish itself in the market.

examples.ko: 한국 영화가 세계 무대에 자리매김한 건 오래되지 않았어요.
examples.en: It hasn't been long since Korean film took its place on the world stage.

examples.ko: 이 축제는 지역 대표 행사로 자리매김할 거예요.
examples.en: This festival will establish itself as the region's signature event.

examples.ko: 천천히 자리매김해 가는 과정이 쉽지 않았어요.
examples.en: The process of slowly establishing itself was not easy.

explain: '자리 잡다'와 비슷하지만 기사나 발표 같은 글에서 더 딱딱하게 들려요. 보통 '~로 자리매김하다'처럼 '(으)로'와 같이 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '자리 잡다'가 더 편해요.
explain_en: It is close to '자리 잡다' but sounds more formal, like in news articles or presentations. It usually comes with '(으)로', as in '~로 자리매김하다' (establish oneself as ~). In everyday conversation, '자리 잡다' is more comfortable.

examples.en: I saw a weasel in the forest.
A weasel got into the chicken coop and the chickens were frightened.
A weasel has a long body and short legs.
I heard that in the past, brushes were made from weasel tail hair.
That child ran away as fast as a weasel.
An animal that looked like a weasel passed by at night.

explain: 몸이 긴 비슷한 동물로 '수달'과 '담비'가 있는데, 족제비가 훨씬 작고 가늘어요. 예전에 시골에서 닭을 잡아먹는 동물로 알려졌고, 꼬리털로는 붓을 만들기도 했어요.
explain_en: Other long-bodied animals like it are the '수달' (otter) and '담비' (marten), but a 족제비 is much smaller and slimmer. In the old countryside it was known as an animal that preyed on chickens, and its tail hair was also used to make brushes.

examples.ko: 주사위를 던져서 나온 수만큼 말을 움직여요.
examples.en: You throw the dice and move your piece by the number that comes up.
The die rolled off onto the floor.
We decided the order with a die instead of rock-paper-scissors.

examples.ko: 보드게임에서 주사위 두 개를 같이 굴려요.
examples.en: In the board game, you roll two dice together.

examples.ko: 주사위에는 일부터 육까지 점이 찍혀 있어요.
examples.en: A die has dots from one to six on it.
I had good luck with the dice this time.

explain: '주사위를 던지다/굴리다'로 말하고, 점이 찍힌 면은 '눈'이라고 해서 '눈이 6이 나왔다'처럼 말해요. 정하기 어려울 때 '주사위를 던져서 정하자'고도 해요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 결정을 했고 돌이킬 수 없다는 뜻이에요. 큰 결정을 하고 나서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means a decision has been made and cannot be reversed. People use it after a big decision.

explain_en: People say '주사위를 던지다/굴리다' (throw/roll the dice), and the dotted faces are called '눈', so you say '눈이 6이 나왔다' (a six came up). When a choice is hard, people also say '주사위를 던져서 정하자' (let's decide by dice).

en: broker; mediate between buyer and seller

examples.en: The real estate agency brokers house deals.
A friend brokered the contract between the two companies.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 여행객과 집주인을 중개하는 서비스예요.
examples.en: This app is a service that connects travelers with homeowners.
You get a fee when you broker a deal.

examples.ko: 집을 중개해 준 사람에게 감사 인사를 했어요.
examples.en: I thanked the person who brokered the house for me.

examples.ko: 중개업자가 집을 중개하고 나서 수수료를 받았어요.
examples.en: The agent received a fee after brokering the house.

explain: 사고파는 사람 사이에서 거래를 이어 줄 때 써요. 다투는 사람들 사이에 끼어 화해시키는 건 '중재하다'라서 서로 달라요. '부동산 중개', '중개 수수료'처럼 쓰는 말이 많아요.
explain_en: It is used when you connect people who buy and sell and help a deal go through. Stepping in between people who are fighting to settle things is '중재하다', which is different. Common combinations are '부동산 중개' (real estate brokerage) and '중개 수수료' (brokerage fee).

examples.en: The construction is progressing as scheduled.
I'm worried because the work isn't progressing well.
I'll let you know right away if the negotiation moves forward.
The project made a lot of progress this week.
I can feel my thesis moving forward little by little.
I reported the progress to the team leader.

explain: 공사, 협상, 연구처럼 시간이 걸리는 일이 앞으로 나아갈 때 써요. '진척이 없다', '진척이 더디다'처럼 부정적인 말과 같이 나올 때가 많아요. 사람이 실력이 느는 건 '발전하다'나 '늘다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is used when a job that takes time, like construction, negotiation, or research, moves forward. It often appears in negative phrases such as '진척이 없다' (no progress) or '진척이 더디다' (progress is slow). When a person improves, use '발전하다' or '늘다'.

examples.en: He proposed to his girlfriend at the beach.
I'll prepare a ring and propose.

examples.ko: 남자 친구가 깜짝 이벤트로 청혼하는 영상을 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched a video of a boyfriend proposing with a surprise event.
Before proposing, I first paid my respects to her parents.
Thank you so much for proposing to me.

examples.ko: 그에게 청혼하고 나서 며칠 동안 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: After proposing to him, I couldn't sleep for several days.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '프러포즈하다'가 더 흔하고, '청혼'은 글이나 뉴스에서 많이 나와요. '청혼을 받다/받아들이다/거절하다'처럼 명사로도 자주 써요.
explain_en: In everyday talk '프러포즈하다' is more common, while '청혼' appears more in writing and the news. The noun is also common: '청혼을 받다/받아들이다/거절하다' (receive/accept/turn down a proposal).

examples.en: I laid a thick carpet in the living room.
The carpet got dirty, so I sent it to the cleaner's.

examples.ko: 아이가 카펫 위에서 블록을 쌓고 있어요.
examples.en: The child is stacking blocks on the carpet.
Dust piles up easily because of the carpet.
The cat sharpens its claws on the carpet.

examples.ko: 이 카펫은 털이 길어서 청소기로 밀기 힘들어요.
examples.en: This rug has long fibers, so it's hard to vacuum.

explain: 방 전체에 까는 건 '카펫', 소파나 침대 앞에 까는 작은 건 '러그'라고 구분해서 말하기도 해요. 한국 집은 바닥이 따뜻한 온돌이라 카펫을 깔지 않는 집도 많아요. '카펫을 깔다', '카펫을 털다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: People sometimes distinguish a '카펫' that covers a whole room from a small '러그' laid in front of a sofa or bed. Many Korean homes have heated ondol floors, so some homes don't use carpet at all. Common phrases are '카펫을 깔다' (lay a carpet) and '카펫을 털다' (shake out a carpet).

examples.en: Two prisoners broke out of jail before dawn.

examples.ko: 영화에서 주인공이 탈옥하는 장면이 인상 깊었어요.
examples.en: The scene where the hero breaks out of prison stood out in the movie.

examples.ko: 그는 감옥에서 탈옥하려고 몇 년 동안 계획을 세웠어요.
examples.en: He planned for years to escape from prison.
I heard the escaped criminal was caught in two days.

examples.ko: 탈옥하고 나서도 마음 편히 지내지 못했어요.
examples.en: Even after escaping prison, he couldn't live in peace.

examples.ko: 탈옥할 방법이 없다는 걸 알고 포기했어요.
examples.en: He gave up when he realized there was no way to break out.

explain: 감옥에서 도망칠 때만 쓰고, 다른 곳에서 빠져나오는 건 '탈출하다'나 '도망치다'를 써요. 뉴스와 영화 줄거리에서 주로 보여요. 발음은 [타로카다]예요.
explain_en: It is only for escaping from a prison; for getting out of other places use '탈출하다' or '도망치다'. You mostly see it in the news and in movie plots. It is pronounced [타로카다].

examples.en: The medication times are morning and evening.

examples.ko: 간호사가 투약 전에 이름을 다시 확인했어요.
examples.en: The nurse rechecked my name before giving the medication.
Wrong medication can be dangerous.
It has been a week since the medication started.

examples.ko: 아이의 투약 기록을 수첩에 적고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm writing my child's medication record in a notebook.

examples.ko: 약국에서 투약 방법을 자세히 설명해 줬어요.
examples.en: The pharmacy explained in detail how to take the medicine.

explain: 병원과 약국에서 쓰는 전문적인 말이에요. 일상에서는 '약을 먹다', '약을 먹이다'라고 해요. '투약 시간', '투약 기록', '투약량'처럼 뒤에 말이 붙는 일이 많아요.
explain_en: This is a technical word used in hospitals and pharmacies. In daily life, people say '약을 먹다' (take medicine) or '약을 먹이다' (give medicine to someone). It often has another word after it, as in '투약 시간', '투약 기록', and '투약량'.

examples.en: The choir's harmony was truly beautiful.
The two voices create a lovely harmony.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 서로 하모니를 이루며 일해요.
examples.en: Our team works together in harmony.
It's a song with a good blend of guitar and piano.

examples.ko: 친구와 노래할 때 하모니를 맞추는 게 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard to match harmony when I sing with a friend.
Today's harmony practice is two hours.

explain: 음악에서는 '화음'이라고도 해요. 사람 사이나 색깔이 어울릴 때는 '조화'가 더 자연스러워요. '하모니를 이루다', '하모니를 맞추다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: In music it is also called '화음'. For people getting along or colors matching, '조화' is more natural. Common phrases are '하모니를 이루다' (form a harmony) and '하모니를 맞추다' (match the harmony).

examples.en: I went to donate blood during vacation.

examples.ko: 저는 두 달에 한 번 헌혈해요.
examples.en: I donate blood once every two months.
After donating blood, I got a snack.

examples.ko: 몸이 안 좋으면 헌혈할 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't donate blood if you feel unwell.
They give a souvenir to people who donated blood.
I was a little nervous the first time I donated blood.

explain: '피를 주다'라고 하지 않고 '헌혈하다'라고 말하고, 명사로 '헌혈을 하다'라고도 해요. 헌혈하는 곳은 '헌혈의 집'이라는 이름이 많아요. 피를 받는 쪽은 '수혈을 받다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Koreans say '헌혈하다' rather than 'give blood', and also use the noun in '헌혈을 하다'. Donation places are often named '헌혈의 집'. The person who receives the blood is said to '수혈을 받다'.

examples.en: The children played in the river, swimming around.
A duck is swimming slowly on the lake.

examples.ko: 헤엄에 자신이 없어서 깊은 곳에는 안 가요.
examples.en: I'm not confident at swimming, so I don't go to deep places.

examples.ko: 헤엄도 못 치는데 바다에 가자고 해요.
examples.en: He wants to go to the sea even though I can't swim.
He moved his arms and legs as if a frog were swimming.

examples.ko: 물이 차가워서 헤엄이 잘 안 돼요.
examples.en: The water is cold, so I can't swim well.

explain: '헤엄'은 사람, 동물, 물고기에게 모두 쓰고 '헤엄을 치다'라고 해요. 운동으로 하는 건 '수영'이라고 해서 '수영 대회'는 되지만 '헤엄 대회'는 어색해요. 놀이나 동물 이야기에 '헤엄'을 많이 써요.
explain_en: '헤엄' is used for people, animals, and fish, and the verb phrase is '헤엄을 치다'. Swimming as a sport is '수영', so '수영 대회' works but '헤엄 대회' sounds odd. '헤엄' is common in talk about play and animals.

examples.en: A weapon was found at the scene of the incident.

examples.ko: 목격자는 흉기를 든 남자를 봤다고 말했어요.
examples.en: A witness said he saw a man holding a weapon.

examples.ko: 가위도 잘못 쓰면 흉기가 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even scissors can become a weapon if misused.

examples.ko: 공항에서는 흉기가 될 수 있는 물건을 가지고 탈 수 없어요.
examples.en: At the airport, you can't carry items that could be used as weapons.
An object suspected of being a weapon came out of the bag.
Carrying a weapon is prohibited by law.

explain: 뉴스와 법 이야기에 나오는 딱딱한 말이에요. 사람을 해치는 데 쓰인 도구를 말하고, 칼이나 망치처럼 원래 다른 용도인 물건도 '흉기'가 될 수 있어요. 일반적으로 싸움 도구를 말할 때는 '무기'를 쓰지만, 사건 이야기에서는 '흉기'를 써요.
explain_en: It is a stiff word found in news and legal talk. It means a tool used to hurt people, and an object made for another purpose, like a knife or hammer, can become a '흉기'. In general talk about fighting tools '무기' is used, but in reports of incidents '흉기' is the usual word.

examples.en: Passengers watched the sea from the deck.
Waves splashed up onto the deck.
The sailors scrubbed the deck clean.
If you go out onto the deck, the wind blows hard.

examples.ko: 크루즈 갑판은 저녁이 되면 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: The cruise ship's deck gets crowded in the evening.

examples.ko: 폭풍이 오기 전에 갑판의 짐을 묶었어요.
examples.en: Before the storm, they tied down the cargo on the deck.

explain: 배 위쪽에 바깥으로 드러난 넓은 바닥이라서 '갑판에 올라가다/나가다'처럼 말해요. 배 안의 방은 '선실'이라고 해서 갑판과 구별해요. 배가 크면 '갑판'이 여러 층일 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is the wide, open-air floor on top of a ship, so people say '갑판에 올라가다/나가다'. A room inside the ship is a '선실', which is different from the deck. A large ship can have several decks.

examples.en: This doll is small and adorable.
My niece came in a cute outfit.
The child waved at me in a charming way.
The cake at that cafe was cute in shape.
The packaging was so cute that I bought it as a gift.
Her way of talking is cute, but she is very sensible inside.

explain: '귀엽다'보다 작고 야무지고 앙증맞은 매력에 써서 큰 동물에는 잘 안 써요. '깜찍한 거짓말'처럼 어린아이의 얄밉고 대담한 행동에 쓰기도 해요. 어른이 귀엽게 행동할 때도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: Compared with '귀엽다', it fits a small, sharp, dainty charm, so it is rarely used for large animals. It can also describe a cheeky, daring act by a child, as in '깜찍한 거짓말' (a cheeky little lie). It can be used for an adult behaving cutely too.

examples.en: A soldier blows the bugle every morning.
When the bugle sounds, everyone gathers.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 나팔처럼 큰 소리로 노래했어요.
examples.en: That child sang as loudly as a trumpet.
A morning glory blooms in the morning and wilts by day.
I bought pants with a flared, trumpet-shaped hem.

examples.ko: 행진할 때 나팔과 북이 같이 울렸어요.
examples.en: During the parade, trumpets and drums sounded together.

explain: 입으로 부는 금속 악기를 말하고 '나팔을 불다'라고 해요. 모양이 닮은 것에 붙여 '나팔꽃', '나팔바지'라고 해요. 오케스트라 악기를 정확히 말할 때는 '트럼펫'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It means a brass instrument blown by mouth, and the verb phrase is '나팔을 불다'. It is attached to things shaped similarly, as in '나팔꽃' (morning glory) and '나팔바지' (flared pants). For the exact orchestral instrument, people say '트럼펫'.

examples.en: My umbrella flipped inside out because of the gust.
A sudden gust blew and my hat flew off.
The forecast said to watch out for gusts in the afternoon.
The child frightened by the gust started crying.
A rookie who appeared out of nowhere won the title.
The sign shook even in a light gust.

explain: 갑자기 세게 불다가 그치는 바람이에요. '태풍'은 열대 바다에서 생겨 큰 비와 함께 오는 큰 폭풍이고, '돌풍'은 짧고 갑작스러운 바람이에요. 뉴스에서는 사람이나 작품이 갑자기 큰 인기를 얻을 때도 '돌풍'을 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 큰 인기나 화제를 모은다는 뜻이에요. 드라마, 가수, 상품에 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means to suddenly gain great popularity or attention. It is used often for dramas, singers, and products.

explain_en: It is a wind that blows hard suddenly and then stops. A '태풍' is a big storm that forms over tropical seas and brings heavy rain, while a '돌풍' is a short, abrupt wind. In the news, '돌풍' is also used when a person or a work suddenly becomes hugely popular.

examples.en: The children go to school at eight in the morning.
It rained today, so I went to school early.
I met a friend on the way to school.
When vacation ends, I'll go to school again.

examples.ko: 등교하고 나서 도시락을 두고 온 걸 알았어요.
examples.en: After arriving at school, I realized I had left my lunchbox.

examples.ko: 늦게 등교한 학생은 교무실에 들러야 해요.
examples.en: Students who arrive late must stop by the staff room.

explain: '학교에 가다'와 거의 같지만 학교와 학생 입장에서 쓰는 격식 있는 말이에요. 반대말은 '하교하다'이고, 회사에 가는 건 '출근하다'예요. '등교 시간', '등교 길'처럼도 써요.
explain_en: It means almost the same as '학교에 가다' but is a more formal word from the standpoint of schools and students. The opposite is '하교하다', and going to work is '출근하다'. It also appears in '등교 시간' (school arrival time) and '등교 길' (the way to school).

examples.en: The lighthouse light twinkles over the night sea.

examples.ko: 섬 끝에 하얀 등대가 서 있어요.
examples.en: A white lighthouse stands at the tip of the island.

examples.ko: 등대를 보고 배가 항구 쪽으로 방향을 잡았어요.
examples.en: The ship set its course toward the harbor by looking at the lighthouse.
The lighthouse keeper turns on the light every night.

examples.ko: 그 선생님은 저에게 인생의 등대 같은 분이에요.
examples.en: That teacher is like a lighthouse in my life.

examples.ko: 등대까지 걸어가는 데 삼십 분쯤 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes about thirty minutes to walk to the lighthouse.

explain: 배가 밤에 길을 찾도록 바닷가에 세우는 탑이에요. 비유로 길을 알려 주는 사람을 '등대 같은 사람'이라고 해요. 등대에서 일하는 사람은 '등대지기'예요.
explain_en: It is a tower built on the coast so ships can find their way at night. Figuratively, someone who shows you the way is called '등대 같은 사람'. A person who works at a lighthouse is a '등대지기'.

examples.ko: 겨울에 모피 코트를 입은 사람이 많았어요.
examples.en: Many people wore fur coats in winter.

examples.ko: 모피를 입지 않는 사람이 점점 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: More and more people don't wear fur.
This shop sells only faux fur.
Fur is warm but hard to take care of.
Be careful not to let water touch the fur.

examples.ko: 할머니가 오래된 모피로 목도리를 만들어 주셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother made me a scarf out of old fur.

explain: 동물의 털가죽으로 만든 옷감이나 옷을 말할 때 써요. 진짜가 아닌 것은 '인조 모피'라고 하고, 동물 몸에 난 털은 그냥 '털'이라고 해요. 동물 보호 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is used for cloth or clothing made from animal pelts. A non-real version is called '인조 모피' (faux fur), and the hair on an animal's body is simply '털'. It comes up often in talk about animal protection.

en: run out of charge; be discharged

examples.en: My phone battery is completely dead.

examples.ko: 폰이 방전돼서 길을 찾을 수 없었어요.
examples.en: My phone ran out of charge, so I couldn't find the way.
The car's battery is dead and it won't start.
Plug in the charger before it runs out of power.

examples.ko: 오래 쓰지 않은 배터리는 저절로 방전돼요.
examples.en: A battery left unused for a long time drains by itself.
Where can I charge a drained power bank?

explain: 배터리나 전기 기구에서 전기가 다 떨어졌을 때 써요. 사람이 너무 지쳤을 때 '완전히 방전됐다'고 농담처럼 말하기도 해요. 반대말은 '충전되다'예요.
explain_en: It is used when a battery or electrical device has run out of electricity. People also joke '완전히 방전됐다' when they are completely worn out. The opposite is '충전되다' (get charged).
